name: Peaceful Pines Campground
summary: Set in North Central Massachusetts off MA-2 in Templeton, Peaceful Pines Campground is a year-round, 120-site RV park offering full-hookup and pump-out sites for seasonal and transient rigs up to 45 feet.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45 ft (120 full-hookup and pump-out RV sites; no tents)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — straightforward highway access off MA-2 via US-202 / Baldwinville Road with wide interior pine-grove lanes
scorecard.treeClearance: Tall white pine canopy throughout; main avenues are well-trimmed for Class As and fifth-wheels, with tighter overhead limbs on perimeter pads
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Avenue Full-Hookup 50-Amp Pull-Through & Long Back-In Sites (up to 45 ft)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Interior Pine Grove & Pond-Adjacent Pads (under 32 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From MA-2 (Route 2) East or West, take Exit 83 (US-202 / Baldwinville Road / Templeton) and follow Baldwinville Road directly to the Peaceful Pines entrance at 2 Peaceful Pines. Avoid unpaved town roads or narrow cut-throughs off Patriots Road.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps large rigs routed cleanly off MA-2 Exit 83 onto Baldwinville Road rather than narrow town cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the wide front check-in parking area off Baldwinville Road before entering the pine-lined interior loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging near the front office and backing into pine-lined RV pads.

content.overview: 120-site year-round RV community in Templeton (roughly 1 hour west of Boston, open for Winter 2026–27 extended stays) featuring full-hookup and pump-out RV sites, saltwater swimming pool, game room and pool hall, fishing pond, and active weekend events.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electrical systems during peak summer air-conditioning loads and winter extended stays.

content.loopC: Wide full-hookup 50-amp sites along the primary avenues accommodating Class As, fifth-wheels, and toy haulers up to 45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Shaded pine-grove and pond-edge sites suited for travel trailers and Class Cs under 32 ft.

name: Highview Campground
address: 58 John Gilbert Rd, West Brookfield, MA 01585
summary: Perched 950 feet above sea level in Central Massachusetts near Lake Wickaboag, Highview Campground is a year-round, RV-only park offering 30-amp open and wooded sites for rigs up to 40 feet.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40 ft (30-amp RV-only sites; no tents)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved approach via MA-32 North, Lyon Road, Ragged Hill Road, and John Gilbert Road with a steady ridge climb
scorecard.treeClearance: Open panoramic ridge sites with generous sky clearance alongside wooded perimeter pads with mature hardwoods
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Open Ridge & Panoramic View 30-Amp Sites (up to 40 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (Mass Pike) Exit 63 (Palmer), take MA-32 North to Lyon Road, continue onto Ragged Hill Road, and turn right onto John Gilbert Road to 58 John Gilbert Rd. Avoid narrow hilltown cut-throughs off Wickaboag Valley Road or unpaved town lanes.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps RVs on the primary MA-32 North, Lyon Road, and Ragged Hill Road approach rather than narrow Central Mass hilltown cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle near the front check-in and entrance pull-off on John Gilbert Road before navigating the ridge loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging near the John Gilbert Road entrance and backing into ridge or wooded sites.

content.overview: Year-round, RV-only hilltop campground sitting at approximately 950 feet elevation in West Brookfield (open for Winter 2026–27 extended stays) featuring 30-amp hookups, panoramic Central Mass views, bonfire area, and proximity to Lake Wickaboag town beach.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV appliances and electronics on 30-amp hookup pedestals during peak summer and winter extended stays.

content.loopC: Open ridge-top 30-amp sites with wider approach angles and clear overhead clearance for Class As, Class Cs, and travel trailers up to 40 ft.
content.loopsAB: Quieter wooded sites tucked along the tree line suited for travel trailers and Class Cs under 32 ft.

name: Circle CG Campground
summary: Positioned right off I-495 on MA-126 in Bellingham, Circle CG Campground is a 30-acre, 150-site year-round RV park offering easy highway access and hookup sites for big rigs up to 45 feet.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 45 ft (30- and 50-amp RV sites; open year-round)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: High — direct frontage on MA-126 (North Main Street) just south of I-495 with a wide entrance apron
scorecard.treeClearance: Open meadow and mixed pine canopy; generous overhead clearance along main entrance spine and big-rig lanes
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Meadow & Front 50-Amp Full-Hookup Sites (up to 45 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Exit I-495 onto MA-126 South (Hartford Avenue / North Main Street) and watch carefully just off the highway—MA-126 makes a left turn at the traffic light to continue south as North Main Street directly to 131 N Main St on the right. Stay on MA-126 through the signal rather than going straight onto local residential roads.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear lane guidance for the immediate MA-126 left turn at the traffic signal just off I-495.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the wide front check-in parking lot directly off MA-126 before proceeding past the office into the interior loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging in the front check-in lot and backing into interior meadow or wooded sites.

content.overview: 30-acre, 150-site year-round family RV park in Bellingham (45 minutes southwest of Boston and 45 minutes from Providence and Cape Cod) featuring 30- and 50-amp hookups, Winter 2026–27 extended-stay availability, swimming pool, gem mining, and horseshoes.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electrical systems on 30- and 50-amp pedestals during summer air-conditioning loads and winter extended stays.

content.loopC: Open, wide-radius 50-amp sites near the main meadow and front section accommodating Class As, fifth-wheels, and toy haulers up to 45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Shaded rear wooded sites suited for travel trailers, Class Cs, and pop-ups under 32 ft.

name: Berry's Grove Campground
summary: Open year-round on the shores of Lake Mascuppic in Tyngsborough just south of the NH border, Berry's Grove Campground offers 24 full-hookup 50-amp RV sites (town water and sewer) with private lake dock access.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40–45 ft (24 RV-only full-hookup 50-amp sites; no tent camping)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — easy highway approach via US-3 Exit 87 onto Westford Road, Kendall Road, and Lakeview Avenue, though residential lakeside streets near Davis Street require careful turning
scorecard.treeClearance: Mature lakeside oaks and maples; watch overhead branches along Davis Street and shoreline pads

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From US-3 North or South, take Exit 87 (Westford Road / Tyngsborough) east across the Merrimack River bridge onto Middlesex Road / Kendall Road, continue onto Lakeview Avenue (MA-113 East) along Lake Mascuppic, and turn onto Davis Street to 35 Davis St. Avoid narrow residential lake-cottage cut-throughs off Willowdale Avenue.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps large rigs on primary MA-113 and Lakeview Avenue connectors rather than narrow Lake Mascuppic cottage lanes.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle near the front check-in and lakeside parking pull-off along Davis Street before backing into your 50-amp pad.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging along Davis Street and backing into lakeside full-hookup pads.

content.overview: Intimate 24-site lakeside RV community on Lake Mascuppic (15 minutes from Nashua, NH and 45 minutes north of Boston) operating year-round—including Winter 2026–27 extended stays—with 50-amp electric, municipal water and sewer hookups, private dock, and swimming area.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics on 50-amp pedestals during summer peak loads and winter extended stays.

content.loopC: Longer interior 50-amp full-hookup pads offering cleaner backing angles for Class As, Class Cs, and fifth-wheels up to 40–45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Tighter lakeside and dock-adjacent pads best suited for travel trailers and Class Cs under 32 ft.

name: Savoy Mountain State Forest Campground
summary: Tucked into a former apple orchard high on the Hoosac Range off MA-2 (Mohawk Trail) in Florida, MA, Savoy Mountain State Forest Campground offers 45 dry-camping sites and a central dump station via South County Road and Central Shaft Road.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 30–35 ft (select orchard loop pads; dry camping only, no hookups)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Challenging — steep 8–10% grades and hairpin turns on MA-2 (Mohawk Trail) require careful gear and brake management plus unhooking at check-in
scorecard.treeClearance: Open orchard canopy in the main camping meadow with dense forest around perimeter pads
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Sites 6–31 & 36–45 (wider former apple orchard sites with easier swing clearance)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Sites 1–5 & 32–35 (shorter wooded perimeter pads best for vans, truck campers, and small trailers under 25 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From MA-2 (Mohawk Trail) in Florida, MA, take Church Road to South County Road, then turn onto Central Shaft Road to the campground entrance (South County Road can also be accessed directly from MA-2 a few miles south of Florida). Do not follow consumer GPS shortcuts onto River Road, Tilda Hill Road, or steep unpaved Savoy backroads, and prepare for the steep grades and hairpin switchbacks on MA-2's Western Summit when climbing eastbound from North Adams.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides grade and hairpin warnings along MA-2 (Mohawk Trail) and keeps RVs on Church Road and South County Road instead of unpaved forest shortcuts.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the wide day-use and check-in parking area on Central Shaft Road just before the campground entrance gate.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when unhooking in the Central Shaft Road staging lot and backing into orchard or perimeter pads.

content.overview: High-elevation northern Berkshire state forest campground set in a historic apple orchard near North Pond, South Pond, Bog Pond, and Tannery Falls, offering 45 primitive sites (no electric, water, or sewer hookups), 4 log cabins, flush-toilet and shower comfort stations, bear boxes, and an RV dump station.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps stabilize travel trailers and motorhomes on sloped former orchard pads.

content.loopC: Former apple orchard meadow sites (Sites 6–31 & 36–45) providing wider turn radii and open sky for self-contained rigs up to 30–35 ft.
content.loopsAB: Wooded edge sites (Sites 1–5 & 32–35) suited for smaller travel trailers, camper vans, and pop-ups under 25 ft.

name: Summit Hill Campground
summary: Perched on the Berkshire plateau in Washington near October Mountain and Pittsfield, Summit Hill Campground offers wooded water/electric RV sites with direct access to on-site hiking trails and high-elevation summer breezes.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 35–40 ft (select open/field-edge RV pads; wooded sites vary)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — hilltown approach via MA-8 and Washington Mountain Road / Old Middlefield Road features sustained 5–7% climbs
scorecard.treeClearance: Mixed plateau hardwoods and pines; open clearing near the main activity field provides good clearance while wooded interior sites have low branches
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Open Plateau & Main Field-Edge RV Sites

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Approach via MA-8 (from Hinsdale/Dalton to the north or Becket/US-20 to the south) onto Washington Mountain Road / Summit Hill Road to 34 Old Middlefield Rd in Washington. Avoid narrow gravel hilltown roads (such as Frost Road or unpaved Middlefield town roads) when towing; verify your exact route via paved MA-8 connectors.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps RVs routed along paved MA-8 plateau connectors rather than steep, narrow hilltown dirt roads.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in parking area off Old Middlefield Road before entering the wooded interior loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging near the Old Middlefield Road check-in lot and backing into wooded pads.

content.overview: High-elevation Berkshire plateau campground in Washington offering water/electric RV sites, secluded tent sites, on-site hiking trails, playground, and family weekend events midway between Lee and Pittsfield.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps stabilize travel trailers and motorhomes on sloped Berkshire plateau terrain.

content.loopC: Wider, flatter plateau sites near the main entrance and central recreation lawn suited for Class Cs, fifth-wheels, and travel trailers up to 35–40 ft.
content.loopsAB: Quiet, heavily wooded perimeter pads tailored to smaller travel trailers, camper vans, and pop-ups under 30 ft.

name: Walker Island Family Camping
summary: Situated right along scenic US-20 (Jacob's Ladder Trail) beside Walker Brook in Chester, Walker Island Family Camping offers 90 wooded 20/30-amp sites tailored to RVs up to 30–38 feet.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 30–38 ft (select outer/field sites up to 38 ft; brookside/island sites capped at 30 ft)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — direct frontage on US-20, though crossing the internal brook bridge and navigating wooded island turns requires unhooking
scorecard.treeClearance: Heavy hemlock and hardwood shade along Walker Brook; check low branches on brookside sites
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Main Entrance & Upper Open 30-Amp Sites (up to 38 ft)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Wooded Walker Brook & Island Sites (under 30 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Take I-90 (Mass Pike) Exit 41 (Westfield) onto US-20 West for approximately 19 miles along the Westfield River valley straight into Chester (27 US-20 on the left), or take I-90 Exit 10 (Lee) east on US-20 over Jacob's Ladder (6% mountain grades—use lower gears on descent) for ~15 miles into Chester.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides grade and curve alerts along US-20 (Jacob's Ladder Scenic Byway) and prevents routing onto steep hilltown cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in lot directly off US-20 before crossing the internal bridge onto the wooded island section.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when unhooking in the US-20 entrance lot and backing onto brookside or island pads.

content.overview: Family-friendly 90-site campground along Walker Brook on historic Jacob's Ladder Scenic Byway (US-20), featuring 20/30-amp water/electric sites, swimming pool, rec hall, laundry, propane, and proximity to Keystone Arch Bridges and Chester-Blandford State Forest.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics from voltage dips and surges on 20- and 30-amp hookup pedestals.

content.loopC: Level 30-amp sites near the main entrance and pool field accommodating Class Cs and travel trailers up to 38 ft.
content.loopsAB: Shaded brookside and island sites tucked under tall hemlocks; strictly suited for rigs 30 ft and under.

name: October Mountain State Forest Campground
summary: Set inside Massachusetts' largest state forest just 3 miles north of I-90 Exit 10 in Lee, October Mountain State Forest Campground offers 44 dry-camping sites across a three-tiered woodland layout with a central dump station.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 35 ft (select lower-tier sites; dry camping only, no hookups)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved approach via US-20, Center Street, and Woodland Road, though tight three-tiered forest loops make unhooking advisable
scorecard.treeClearance: Dense northern hardwood canopy across all three tiers; inspect overhead branches carefully before raising roof vents or awnings
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Lower Tier Sites 1–23 (longer gravel pads near the main access road and dump station)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Upper Tier Sites 24–28 & 34–50 (tighter turn radii best for vans, truck campers, and trailers under 25 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (Mass Pike) Exit 10 (Lee), follow US-20 West 1.1 miles into downtown Lee, turn north onto Center Street, and continue onto Woodland Road to 256 Woodland Rd. Do not follow GPS shortcuts over unpaved Washington Mountain Road or steep gravel forest service roads from Becket or Washington—use the paved Lee approach exclusively.

recommendedGear.reason: Prevents routing RVs onto steep, unpaved Washington Mountain Road forest shortcuts.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle at the campground entrance and visitor contact parking area off Woodland Road before climbing the three-tiered loop road.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when unhooking at the Woodland Road entrance and backing into wooded gravel pads.

content.overview: 17,000-acre Massachusetts DCR state forest campground featuring 44 primitive campsites (no water, electric, or sewer hookups), 3 yurts, hot-shower comfort stations, bear-proof food lockers, an RV dump station, and direct access to Schermerhorn Gorge and the Appalachian Trail.

recommendedGear.reason: Essential for leveling RVs and travel trailers on sloped, terraced woodland gravel pads.

content.loopC: Lower-tier sites (Sites 1–23) offering the widest approach angles and straightest back-in pads for self-contained RVs up to 35 ft.
content.loopsAB: Higher-elevation terraced sites (Sites 24–50) with tighter switchbacks and shorter gravel pads suited for camper vans, pop-ups, and small trailers under 25 ft.

name: Camp Overflow
summary: Positioned along the 3-mile Otis Reservoir in East Otis, Camp Overflow offers 150 wooded and lakeside RV sites with water/electric hookups for rigs up to 45 feet via Reservoir Road or West Shore Road onto Tolland Road.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved local connectors via Reservoir Rd (from MA-8) or W Shore Rd (from MA-23) to Tolland Rd, with rolling grades and lakeside loop turns
scorecard.treeClearance: Tall white pine and hemlock canopy around Otis Reservoir; watch low limbs on waterfront back-in pads
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Upper Ridge & Open 30/50-Amp Pull-Through/Long Back-In Sites (up to 45 ft)
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Shoreline Cove & Pine Grove Sites (under 32 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From MA-8, take Reservoir Road west to Tolland Road south directly to 700 Tolland Rd. If approaching from MA-23, take West Shore Road east to Tolland Road south. Watch rolling southern Berkshire grades along the reservoir connectors and avoid narrow seasonal cottage lanes.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps large rigs on the primary Reservoir Road and West Shore Road connectors rather than tight Otis Reservoir cottage roads.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in and marina/store parking area off Tolland Road before descending toward the lakeside loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when unhooking at the Tolland Road entrance and backing into pine-lined pads.

content.overview: Classic southern Berkshire lakefront campground on Otis Reservoir featuring 150 sites, on-site marina, boat rentals, sandy beach, dishwashing station, laundry room, and camp store.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps level motorhomes and travel trailers on sloped lakeside and terraced reservoir pads.

content.loopC: Wider upper-terrace sites with easier turn radii and level pads supporting RVs up to 45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Scenic pine-shaded lakeside and cove sites suited for travel trailers, Class Cs, and pop-ups under 32 ft.

name: Fernwood Forest Campground
summary: Spanning 115 acres of Berkshire woodland adjacent to the Appalachian Trail in Hinsdale, Fernwood Forest Campground offers 20/30/50-amp sites for RVs up to 40 feet with clean access via Michaels Road to Longview Avenue.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved approach via MA-8 South of Hinsdale onto Michaels Rd and Longview Ave
scorecard.treeClearance: Dense 115-acre forest setting; open rec-hall field sites have clean sky while interior forest pads require branch checks
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: 50-Amp Open Field & Main Entrance Loop Sites (up to 40 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Do not route through Hinsdale center when towing. Instead, approach from south of Hinsdale off MA-8 onto Michaels Road, then turn onto Longview Avenue where the campground entrance is right there at 350 Longview Ave. Stick to paved state routes (MA-8 / US-20) and avoid unpaved hilltown roads between Washington and Hinsdale.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps keep large RVs off narrow Hinsdale center streets and unpaved hilltown cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the open staging area near the main office and recreation hall right off the Longview Avenue entrance before backing into wooded sites.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging near the recreation hall and backing into tree-lined pads.

content.overview: Quiet, family-operated 51-site campground on 115 wooded acres bordering the Appalachian Trail, offering 20/30/50-amp hookups, recreation hall, two pavilions, volleyball and basketball courts, and central access to Pittsfield, Tanglewood, and Mt. Greylock.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics against voltage fluctuations on rural 30- and 50-amp pedestals.

content.loopC: Level 50-amp sites near the central recreation hall and open field area accommodating rigs up to 40 ft.
content.loopsAB: Deeply shaded woodland sites tucked along the forest ridge near the Appalachian Trail corridor; best for travel trailers and Class Cs under 30 ft.

name: Mt. Greylock Campsite Park
summary: Set on 40 wooded acres at the base of Massachusetts' highest peak in Lanesborough, Mt. Greylock Campsite Park welcomes RVs up to 38 feet with water/electric hookups and direct US-7 approach routing.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — paved US-7 approach to North Main Street / Scott Road, transitioning to wooded foothill park lanes
scorecard.treeClearance: Mature northern Berkshire hardwood and hemlock canopy; check roof/AC clearance on inner wooded sites
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: Front Open Field & Outer Perimeter Water/Electric Sites (up to 38 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Follow US-7 North or South into Lanesborough, turn east onto North Main Street / Old State Road following campground signage onto Scott Road to 15 Scott Rd. Never tow an RV up Notch Road or Rockwell Road onto the Mt. Greylock Summit auto road—those mountain grades have sharp hairpins, steep 10%+ grades, and strict length and brake restrictions.

recommendedGear.reason: Prevents routing large RVs onto steep Mt. Greylock summit auto roads or narrow mountain cut-throughs.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle near the front office and dump-station staging lane off Scott Road before heading into the sloped, tree-lined interior loops.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when unhooking at the Scott Road entrance lane and backing into wooded foothill pads.

content.overview: Family-run 115-site campground on 40 acres at the foot of Mt. Greylock featuring water/electric hookup sites, dump station, camp store, playground, and immediate trail access to Mt. Greylock State Reservation.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps stabilize travel trailers and motorhomes on sloped lower-mountain foothill pads.

content.loopC: Wider, flatter perimeter and field-adjacent RV sites equipped for rigs up to 38 ft.
content.loopsAB: Secluded, shaded woodland sites nestled along the lower slope of Mt. Greylock; ideal for travel trailers and Class Cs under 30 ft.

name: Bonnie Brae Campground
summary: Located in northern Pittsfield just off US-7 near Lake Pontoosuc, Bonnie Brae Campground offers 30- and 50-amp full-hookup RV sites accommodating rigs up to 45 feet with straightforward arterial highway access.

scorecard.toadFriendliness: Good — direct turn off US-7 onto Broadway Street with level staging near check-in
scorecard.treeClearance: Moderate canopy on perimeter sites; open sky around the central pool and open RV section

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: From I-90 (Mass Pike) Exit 10 (Lee), take US-7 / US-20 North through Pittsfield, continuing north on US-7 (North Street / Wahconah Street corridor) to Broadway Street on the west side near Lake Pontoosuc. Avoid residential cut-through streets in downtown Pittsfield when towing long fifth-wheels or Class As.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps Class A motorhomes and fifth-wheels routed strictly along US-7 through Pittsfield instead of narrow residential side streets.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in parking area at the end of Broadway Street before maneuvering onto your RV pad.

recommendedGear.reason: Provides clear rear visibility when staging at the end of Broadway Street and backing onto full-hookup pads.

content.overview: Quaint ~50-site northern Pittsfield park near Lake Pontoosuc featuring 30/50-amp full-hookup RV sites, heated pool, rec room, laundry, bathhouse, cabins, and easy access to Tanglewood, Hancock Shaker Village, and Pittsfield cultural venues.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics against summer peak voltage fluctuations on 30- and 50-amp full-hookup pedestals.

content.loopC: Level 30/50-amp full-hookup RV pads in the main open section capable of handling rigs up to 45 ft.
content.loopsAB: Cozy shaded sites and tent/cabin edges best suited for smaller travel trailers, camper vans, and Class Cs under 30 ft.

name: Sandy Pond Campground
summary: Tucked in the pine woods of South Plymouth just 3 miles north of the Cape Cod Canal, Sandy Pond Campground offers over 200 wooded campsites with 20/30/50-amp full hookups and easy MA-3 and US-6 access without crossing the Cape Cod bridges.

scorecard.maxRigLength: Up to 40+ ft (select 50-amp full-hookup pull-through and open sites; wooded back-in loops vary)
scorecard.toadFriendliness: Moderate — straightforward paved approach off MA-3 and Bourne Road, though internal pine-loop turns tighten near the pond
scorecard.treeClearance: Dense South Plymouth pitch-pine and oak canopy across most loops; verify overhead branch and slide-out clearance on wooded back-in pads
scorecard.bestBigRigLoops: 50-Amp Full-Hookup Pull-Through & Main Entrance Field Sites
scorecard.bestSmallRigLoops: Shaded Pond-Side & Wooded 30-Amp Back-In Sites (under 30 ft)

approach.title: Highway Approach & Routing Guidance
approach.text: Take MA-3 South toward the Sagamore Bridge and Cape Cod Canal, exiting onto US-6 / MA-3A toward Bourne and Plymouth, or approach via I-495 South to MA-25 East and exit before the Bourne Bridge onto Head of the Bay Road / Bourne Road north into South Plymouth to 834 Bourne Rd. Staying on the mainland side of the Cape Cod Canal avoids Sagamore and Bourne Bridge traffic bottlenecks and tight Cape village roads—avoid unpaved Myles Standish State Forest fire roads when towing.

recommendedGear.reason: Keeps large rigs on paved state connectors off MA-3 and I-495 while avoiding unpaved Myles Standish forest roads.

toadStrategy.text: Unhook your towed vehicle in the front check-in and staging area immediately off Bourne Road before entering the wooded interior loops, as mature pine trees and sandy loop corners make backing with a toad attached tight.

recommendedGear.reason: Helps spot low pine branches and narrow tree trunks when backing into shaded South Plymouth sites.

content.overview: Family-focused Modern America Campgrounds retreat set around a spring-fed pond 3 miles from the Cape Cod Canal and 15 minutes from historic downtown Plymouth, featuring 200+ sites (20/30/50-amp full hookups, cable, and Wi-Fi), a sandy freshwater beach, swimming, bass fishing, canoe and kayak access, jumping pillow, GaGa ball, recreation hall, and arcade.

recommendedGear.reason: Protects RV electronics against summer coastal and Cape-area peak power demand on 30A/50A pedestals.

content.loopC: Larger 50-amp full-hookup pull-through and wider perimeter sites closer to the main entrance and recreation hall, built for Class A motorhomes, Class Cs, and fifth-wheels needing easier swing clearance.
content.loopsAB: Classic shaded pine-forest back-in sites near Sandy Pond's shoreline and beach; best suited for travel trailers, Class Cs under 30 ft, and pop-ups seeking deep shade and pond access.
